candidates.title: Opportunities and challenges for ChatGPT and large language models in biomedicine and health
candidates.summary: Survey of ChatGPT and other LLMs across biomedical information retrieval, extraction, question answering and summarization; concludes LLMs have not yet revolutionized biomedicine and flags fabricated information as a key risk.
candidates.reason: General survey of LLMs for biomedical information extraction to frame the introduction.

candidates.title: A Review on Scientific Knowledge Extraction using Large Language Models in Biomedical Sciences
candidates.summary: PRISMA-style review of LLMs for biomedical evidence synthesis and data extraction; identifies hallucination and weak generalization and calls for unified benchmarks.
candidates.reason: Review of LLM-based knowledge extraction and evidence synthesis in biomedicine.

candidates.title: Performance of large language models in data extraction for evidence synthesis: A systematic review
candidates.summary: Systematic review of studies measuring LLM performance on data extraction for evidence synthesis (J Biomed Inform, 2026).
candidates.reason: Systematic review of LLM data extraction for evidence synthesis, directly matching the focus.

candidates.title: A systematic review on the generative AI applications in human medical genetics
candidates.summary: Systematic review of generative AI and transformer models in human medical genetics, with variant identification, annotation and interpretation a major focus across rare and common diseases.
candidates.reason: Systematic review of LLMs in rare-disease and medical genomics.

candidates.title: Improving automated deep phenotyping through large language models using retrieval-augmented generation
candidates.summary: RAG-HPO assigns HPO terms to published case reports with LLMs; on 120 case reports with 1,792 manual HPO terms it outperformed Doc2HPO, ClinPhen and FastHPOCR (F1 0.80 with Llama-3 70B in the preprint).
candidates.reason: LLM HPO extraction from published rare-disease case reports: the closest prior phenotype-extraction work.

candidates.title: Enhancing phenotype recognition in clinical notes using large language models: PhenoBCBERT and PhenoGPT
candidates.summary: Introduces PhenoBCBERT and PhenoGPT for HPO phenotype recognition in clinical notes of genetic diseases; they identified more phenotype concepts than PhenoTagger.
candidates.reason: Prior LLM HPO-term extraction work the gap statement contrasts with.

candidates.title: Systematic benchmarking demonstrates large language models have not reached the diagnostic accuracy of traditional rare-disease decision support tools
candidates.summary: Benchmarks LLMs on 5,213 published case reports encoded as phenopackets with HPO and Mondo; LLMs did not reach the diagnostic accuracy of Exomiser-style decision support tools.
candidates.reason: LLMs in rare-disease genomics using literature-derived phenopackets.

candidates.title: A corpus of GA4GH Phenopackets: case-level phenotyping for genomic diagnostics and discovery
candidates.summary: Introduces Phenopacket Store: 6,668 phenopackets for 475 Mendelian and chromosomal diseases (423 genes, 3,834 alleles) curated by hand from 959 publications (v0.1.19).
candidates.reason: The phenopacket-store resource named in the hook; shows hand curation covers a small share of cases.

candidates.title: The GA4GH Phenopacket schema defines a computable representation of clinical data
candidates.summary: Describes the GA4GH Phenopacket schema v2, a standard for exchanging case-level phenotype, disease and genotype data using ontologies such as HPO.
candidates.reason: Output format standard referenced when introducing case-level genotype-phenotype records.

candidates.title: Large Language Models for Variant-Centric Functional Evidence Mining
candidates.summary: Builds a benchmark from ClinGen-curated variants to test LLM screening and evidence extraction from literature for variant interpretation, and proposes a human-in-the-loop pipeline (AcmGENTIC).
candidates.reason: Recent LLM variant-literature extraction work evaluated against curated databases.

candidates.title: PubMind: Literature-Based Genetic Variant Extraction and Functional Annotation Using Large Language Models
candidates.summary: LLM framework that extracts variant-disease-pathogenicity relationships from the literature, aimed at gaps in ClinVar coverage (bioRxiv preprint).
candidates.reason: LLM variant extraction from literature motivated by ClinVar gaps, the closest variant-side prior work.

candidates.title: An artificial intelligence framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
candidates.summary: RARE-PHENIX extracts clinical features with LLMs, maps them to HPO and ranks diagnostically informative phenotypes, outperforming PhenoBERT in external validation.
candidates.reason: Recent LLM rare-disease phenotype extraction pipeline.

candidates.title: RareBench: Can LLMs Serve as Rare Diseases Specialists?
candidates.summary: Benchmark evaluating LLMs on rare-disease tasks including phenotype extraction and differential diagnosis.
candidates.reason: Benchmark of LLM capability in rare disease, including phenotype extraction.

section: Related Work: 2.2 LLM-assisted systematic review and verification of claims against cited evidence

candidates.title: Data extraction for evidence synthesis using a large language model: A proof-of-concept study
candidates.summary: Proof-of-concept study in which human reviewers checked data elements extracted by Claude 2 from published studies.
candidates.reason: Human-audited LLM data extraction for evidence synthesis.

candidates.title: Performance of two large language models for data extraction in evidence synthesis
candidates.summary: Compared Claude 2 and GPT-4 extracting prespecified data elements from 10 published articles against human extraction; Claude 2 96.3% accurate, GPT-4 with a PDF plug-in 68.8%; concludes humans should check LLM extractions.
candidates.reason: Example of a small-sample human audit of LLM extraction accuracy.

candidates.title: From promise to practice: challenges and pitfalls in the evaluation of large language models for data extraction in evidence synthesis
candidates.summary: Discusses methodological challenges and pitfalls in evaluating LLM data extraction for evidence synthesis (BMJ Evidence-Based Medicine).
candidates.reason: Directly addresses how extraction accuracy should be audited, supporting the hypothesis about weak evaluation designs.

candidates.title: Performance of large language models in data extraction for evidence synthesis: A systematic review
candidates.summary: Systematic review of studies measuring LLM performance on data extraction for evidence synthesis (J Biomed Inform, 2026).
candidates.reason: Aggregates how LLM extraction accuracy has been measured, including sample sizes and units of audit.

candidates.title: AI-driven evidence synthesis: data extraction of randomized controlled trials with large language models
candidates.summary: Evaluates LLM data extraction from randomized controlled trials against human extraction (International Journal of Surgery, 2025).
candidates.reason: Human-referenced accuracy of LLM extraction for systematic reviews.

candidates.title: Collaborative large language models for automated data extraction in living systematic reviews
candidates.summary: Two LLMs simulating a two-reviewer workflow extract data for living systematic reviews, with agreement-based escalation, evaluated against human extraction.
candidates.reason: LLM extraction with cross-checking evaluated against human reference labels.

candidates.title: Automating the data extraction process for systematic reviews using GPT-4o and o3
candidates.summary: GPT-4o and o3 extraction for systematic reviews; accuracy higher for string than numeric variables, with an adjusted method reaching 96.3% on an external dataset.
candidates.reason: Recent human-checked LLM extraction accuracy study.

candidates.title: ChatGPT-4o can serve as the second rater for data extraction in systematic reviews
candidates.summary: Compared ChatGPT-4o data extraction with two human reviewers and found high validity and reproducibility, positioning it as a second rater.
candidates.reason: LLM extraction validated against human raters.

candidates.title: Critical Assessment of Large Language Models' (ChatGPT) Performance in Data Extraction for Systematic Reviews: Exploratory Study
candidates.summary: ChatGPT extracted 60 data elements from COVID-19 modeling studies with 72% overall accuracy, better on explicit than subjective items.
candidates.reason: Small-sample human audit of LLM extraction showing variable accuracy.

candidates.title: Exploring the use of a Large Language Model for data extraction in systematic reviews: a rapid feasibility study
candidates.summary: Rapid feasibility study of GPT-4 data extraction for systematic reviews; participant and intervention fields accurate, outcomes and study design harder; suggests LLMs as second or third reviewers.
candidates.reason: Human-checked LLM extraction feasibility study.

section: Related Work: 2.2 LLM-assisted systematic review and verification of claims against cited evidence

candidates.title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
candidates.summary: GPT-4 as judge reaches over 80% agreement with human preferences, similar to human-human agreement; documents position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases.
candidates.reason: Core study validating LLM judges against human labels and naming self-enhancement bias.

candidates.title: LLM Evaluators Recognize and Favor Their Own Generations
candidates.summary: LLMs can recognize their own outputs, and self-recognition ability correlates linearly with self-preference bias in evaluation.
candidates.reason: Evidence that verifiers can favour outputs of their own model family.

candidates.title: Self-Preference Bias in LLM-as-a-Judge
candidates.summary: Proposes a fairness-based metric for self-preference bias and finds GPT-4 shows significant self-preference, possibly driven by familiarity (low perplexity) of texts.
candidates.reason: Quantifies same-model favouritism in LLM judges.

candidates.title: Who Validates the Validators? Aligning LLM-Assisted Evaluation of LLM Outputs with Human Preferences
candidates.summary: LLM-based evaluators inherit model flaws and need human grading to align them; introduces EvalGen and the notion of criteria drift.
candidates.reason: Argues LLM verifiers must be calibrated against human labels.

candidates.title: FActScore: Fine-grained Atomic Evaluation of Factual Precision in Long Form Text Generation
candidates.summary: Splits generations into atomic facts and scores the share supported by a knowledge source; validates an automated estimator against human annotations.
candidates.reason: Fine-grained claim-support scoring with an LLM estimator validated against humans.

candidates.title: MiniCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of LLMs on Grounding Documents
candidates.summary: Small fact-checking models reach GPT-4 accuracy at checking claims against grounding documents; introduces the human-labelled LLM-AggreFact benchmark.
candidates.reason: Claim-versus-source verifier evaluated on human-labelled benchmark data, analogous to the gatekeeper.

candidates.title: Automatic Evaluation of Attribution by Large Language Models
candidates.summary: Defines attribution error types and compares prompted LLMs with fine-tuned smaller models as attribution evaluators (AttrScore).
candidates.reason: LLM attribution judges evaluated against labelled data.

candidates.title: AttributionBench: How Hard is Automatic Attribution Evaluation?
candidates.summary: Benchmark compiled from human-annotated attribution datasets showing automatic attribution evaluation remains hard even for state-of-the-art LLMs.
candidates.reason: Shows LLM attribution judges disagree with human labels.

candidates.title: Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines
candidates.summary: Human audit of four generative search engines: only 51.5% of sentences fully supported by citations and 74.5% of citations supported their sentence.
candidates.reason: Human audit of whether cited evidence supports generated statements (citation precision/recall).

candidates.title: TRUE: Re-evaluating Factual Consistency Evaluation
candidates.summary: Standardizes 11 human-annotated datasets to evaluate factual-consistency metrics at the example level; NLI and QG-QA approaches perform best.
candidates.reason: Example-level validation of automatic consistency checkers against human labels.

candidates.title: Verifying Facts in Patient Care Documents Generated by Large Language Models Using Electronic Health Records
candidates.summary: Evaluates an LLM-based system that verifies facts in LLM-generated patient care documents against electronic health records, compared with clinician labels (NEJM AI, 2026).
candidates.reason: Medical-domain LLM fact verifier validated against human labels.

section: 3. Methodology - 3.2 Extraction with provenance and three-state phenotypes

candidates.title: The Claude 3 Model Family: Opus, Sonnet, Haiku
candidates.summary: Anthropic model card (March 2024) introducing the Claude 3 family: Opus (most capable), Sonnet and Haiku. Available at https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/de8ba9b01c9ab7cbabf5c33b80b7bbc618857627/Model_Card_Claude_3.pdf.
candidates.reason: Primary technical report introducing the Claude model family including Claude Opus; no DOI or arXiv id exists.

candidates.title: A Coefficient of Agreement for Nominal Scales
candidates.summary: Introduces kappa, a chance-corrected coefficient of agreement between two raters on nominal scales (Educational and Psychological Measurement 20(1):37-46).
candidates.reason: Original source of Cohen's kappa, used for per-pair rater agreement.

section: 4. Experiments - 4.8 O4 and O5: bias arm, memorization and the open-weight comparison

candidates.title: ROUGE: A Package for Automatic Evaluation of Summaries
candidates.summary: Introduces ROUGE-N, ROUGE-L, ROUGE-W and ROUGE-S for scoring generated summaries against human references (Text Summarization Branches Out, ACL 2004, pp. 74-81; ACL Anthology W04-1013).
candidates.reason: Original source of ROUGE-L used in the memorization probe.

section: 4. Experiments - 4.8 O4 and O5: bias arm, memorization and the open-weight comparison

candidates.title: Controlling the False Discovery Rate: A Practical and Powerful Approach to Multiple Testing
candidates.summary: Introduces the false discovery rate and the step-up procedure that controls it (J R Stat Soc B 57(1):289-300; JSTOR DOI 10.2307/2346101).
candidates.reason: Source of the Benjamini-Hochberg correction applied to the GPSEA tests.

section: 4. Experiments - 4.9 Beside the registered study: extension, Majeed and the corpus addendum

candidates.title: Docling Technical Report
candidates.summary: Introduces Docling, an MIT-licensed open-source PDF conversion package using layout-analysis (DocLayNet) and table-structure models, exporting to JSON or Markdown.
candidates.reason: Primary paper introducing Docling, used to convert PDF free copies.
